source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of solvents for NMR (PDF 203).

blocks.text: 1H NMR mein sample solvent ki zyada miqdar mein ghola jata hai. Aam solvents mein hydrogen atoms hote hain jo tez signals de kar sample ke spectrum mein rukawat dalte: agar aam CHCl3 use ho to is ke akele proton ka signal itna bara hoga ke sample ke kamzor signals chhup jayein. Is liye CDCl3 (deuterated chloroform) ya CD3OD (deuterated methanol) jaise deuterated solvents use hote hain. CDCl3 mein hydrogen ki jagah us ka isotope deuterium (D) hai, jise palatne ke liye mukhtalif radio frequency chahiye, is liye yeh na use hone wali radio waves jazb karta na 1H spectrum mein peak deta hai. Solvent 'khamosh' rehta aur sirf sample ke signals dikhte hain.

blocks.prompt: 1H NMR ke liye CHCl3 ki jagah CDCl3 solvent kyun use hota hai?
blocks.explanation: Deuterium proton ki frequency par jazb nahi karta, is liye CDCl3 sample ke signals chhupane wali peak nahi deta; CHCl3 ka bara proton signal unhein chhupa deta.

items: Deuterated solvents (CDCl3, CD3OD) 1H signal nahi dete: solvent 'khamosh'.
